Subject: Security addendum + breach sub-limit

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Legal ran the Order Form and the Security Addendum past our counsel. They are willing to sign but asked for a carve-out: a breach-specific sub-limit for liabilities tied to data incidents (and explicit exclusion of consequential damages for downstream analytics claims). They want the sub-limit to be a separate cap (25% of the Order Form value, up to $500k) and to have the security addendum call it out so it's not folded into general MSA caps.

Can Redwood accommodate that structure? If possible, please share a redline we can take to our GC. We are under a tight procurement window (need counter-signature by 5/20).

Appreciate a quick turnaround.

— Alex
Sr. Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com

Date: 2027-05-12T08:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security addendum + breach sub-limit

Team — reviewed Acme's ask. High level: we can structure a breach-specific sub-limit but need to preserve core MSA protections. Proposed approach:

1) Security Addendum, new Section 6.3 (Breach Liability Sub-Limit): 
   • "Notwithstanding the Limitation of Liability in Section 11 of the MSA, for losses directly resulting from a Security Incident as defined in this Addendum, Customer's aggregate liability shall be limited to the lesser of (a) twenty-five percent (25%) of the total Order Form fees invoiced in the twelve (12) months preceding the incident and (b) Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (USD $500,000)."

2) Consequential damages: provide explicit carve-out language in the Security Addendum that consequential damages are excluded in the same way as the MSA, but include a narrow exception for third-party claims where Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct is proven.

3) Interplay clause: a short sentence indicating the Sub-Limit is "in addition to, and shall not enlarge, any remedies expressly provided in the Security Addendum or the MSA" — this preserves our ability to rely on indemnities for third-party claims.

Risks / asks for commercial: if we accept a hard cap of $500k there is revenue at risk for larger deployments. Suggest Vivek evaluate whether we need: (a) holdback language tied to SOC2 evidence (reduces fixed cap), or (b) tiered caps for >$5M ARR customers.

I drafted redlines and placed them into the attached MSA_redlines_for_ACME.docx and a marked Security Addendum (Redwood_Security_Addendum_v3.pdf). Please review and sign off so we can send to Acme counsel.

— Priya
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_redlines_for_ACME.docx; Redwood_Security_Addendum_v3.pdf

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security addendum + breach sub-limit

Priya — thanks, this framing looks fine from a product/commercial lens. Quick notes:
- The requested 25% / $500k cap is borderline for the scale of this opportunity (ACME initial commit ~$1.2M ARR). It is acceptable with the following mitigations:
  1) Include a clause that allows upward adjustment of the sub-limit if usage/Order Form value increases > 50% within 12 months.
  2) Add an evidence gating clause: full breach remedy applies only after documented SOC2 Type II or equivalent controls evidence delivered; provisional remediation steps and credits can be used pre-evidence.

If we get buy-in on those, I can accept 25%/500k. Otherwise propose 30%/750k. Either way, I recommend we keep an escape for enterprise legal review for larger deals.

Soojin — ready for me to send a commercial note to Alex with the 25%/500k + the two mitigations above? I can frame it as a balanced concession for a fast procurement path.

— Vivek

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Alex Morrison <alex.morrison@acme-analytics.com>, contracts@acme-analytics.com

Date: 2027-05-13T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security addendum + breach sub-limit — Redwood redlines attached

Alex — thanks for waiting. Attached are: (1) marked Security Addendum with a standalone breach sub-limit (Redwood_Security_Addendum_v3.pdf), and (2) a redlined MSA showing interplay language and consequential damage carve-outs (MSA_redlines_for_ACME.docx). Key points we proposed:

- Breach sub-limit: 25% of 12-month Order Form fees up to $500,000 (explicit in Addendum Section 6.3).
- Consequential damages: excluded per MSA; Addendum includes a narrow exception where Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct is established.
- Two commercial mitigations: (1) automatic review and potential cap adjustment if Order Form value increases >50% in 12 months; (2) remediation/evidence gating tied to SOC2 Type II or equivalent — remedial credits available earlier, full monetary remedies only after evidence delivery.

Please review and let me know if your GC wants specific wording changes. If this matches Acme's internal risk appetite, happy to open DocuSign once legal confirms. Targeting procurement sign-off by 5/20 per your timeline.
